questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I chose Sydney as destination because Australia has a different legal system than Denmark. I have no doubt that this aspect will benefit me in my future career. In addition to the professional aspect, Australia as a country offers a lot of experiences that are not found elsewhere in the world. By choosing Sydney as my destination, I knew that I would not only experience living in a "real" metropolis but also have ample opportunities for enjoying nature. 
Furthermore, Australia was a perfect choice for me because I wanted to be out on my own. The time difference between Australia and Denmark automatically forces you to be more present and figure things out for yourself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found that the university in the host country had prepared me well for my arrival in Australia. Australia has specific requirements and procedures for entry, so it was helpful that the university had provided various materials to read through before I departed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance when I arrived at my study destination.

Additional comments
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing situation in Sydney is very critical after the pandemic, making it difficult to obtain a comprehensive overview. However, we were fortunate to find accommodation through Airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is where you get the best Australian experience, as you actually get to live where the Australians themselves reside. This provides a whole different understanding and experience of the city.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a very confusing process, but luckily the university has an entire department dedicated to assisting exchange students, making it easy to get help and resolve any issues that arose.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university has a dedicated department ready to assist.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses I wanted to take were never offered, which was unfortunate. However, I ended up with some courses that I still found satisfactory.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for it to be a difficult process and have plenty of alternative courses ready in case the ones you prefer are not offered.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level varied significantly from course to course. In courses where there were primarily exchange students, I found the level to be low. In courses with Australian students, I perceived the level to be higher but still lower than in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very different from that at UCPH. Class participation often contributed to one's grade, so the students were much more active than back home. Additionally, we had a lot of supplementary online teaching material, which was helpful. Furthermore, all the teaching was in the form of seminars, and we did not have any lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Justice 
Principles of Public International Law 
Dispute Resolution
Trade Marks Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Justice was completely different from any other legal course I have experienced at UCPH. Trade Marks Law was a challenging but fun course, and the instructors were really excellent.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At the university, there were all kinds of associations and activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
UTS Law Students' Society, UTS Tennis Club, UTS Build (Global leadership program). 
I personally benefitted from these associations as they provided a network within the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Australia has a lot to offer. Personally, I visited Melbourne and went on a road trip down the Great Ocean Road as well as a road trip up the East Coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of things happening in Sydney, and there are ample opportunities to be part of various sports clubs, and more. Therefore, I found it easy to adapt as there were constantly new experiences to be had.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I personally joined two running clubs where there were only Australians. It was the best way for me to make friends with people from Australia.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very open and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Sign up for all sorts of events during the first few weeks to get to know people from different fields of study. 
2. Take the time to plan your assignements and deadlines, so you know when you can travel. 
3. Be open to different cultures.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The entire experience was incredibly rewarding, both academically and personally.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from home has its ups and downs.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.
